newsitem.title: USA: Stocks set more records, aided by techs, banks.
newsitem.headline: Stocks set more records, aided by techs, banks.

text.p: Stocks shattered more records Wednesday, aided by renewed vigour in technology shares and follow-though buying in financial issues and other big blue-chip names.

"The market keeps chugging ahead. The driving force is the market has been basically moving higher every year for six years and it's fairly magnetic to investors," said Gail Dudack, chief investment strategist at UBS Securities.

The Dow Jones industrial average rose 29.07 to 5,933.97, handily topping Tuesday's record close of 5,904.90. In the broader market, advancing issues outpaced decliners by 1,630 to 762 with 439 million shares traded on the New York Stock Exchange.
After closing above 5,900 for the first time Tuesday, "we're reaching for the 6,000 mark. At this rate, we can get there by the end of the week," said Ken Ducey, director of trading at BT Brokerage.

The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks notched its third consecutive all-time high finish, up 4.93 to 694.01. The NYSE Composite index posted its fifth straight record, up 2.36 to 370.54. The average price per share rose 25 cents.

The technology-rich Nasdaq Composite index, which shed 8.54 points over the past two sessions, rallied 14.60 to 1,236.11. That drew the index closer to its record closing high of 1,249.15, set June 5.

Stocks were supported by continued strength in the bond market. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose nearly half a point, knocking its yield down to 6.84 percent -- the lowest since Aug. 22 -- from 6.88 percent at Tuesday's close.
Stronger technology issues included International Business Machines Corp., up 2-1/4 to 125-3/4, BMC Software, up 6-3/4 to 86-1/2, and Intel Corp., up 3-1/4 to 99.

Among financial stocks, Citicorp rose 7/8 to 92-3/8 after reaching a one-year high of 92-7/8. Chase Manhattan added 1/4 to 80-3/4 after touching a 52-week high of 81-3/8, and Sallie Mae gained 4-3/4 to 83-1/4.
Wall Street took Wednesday's only economic release in stride. August U.S. construction spending rose 0.9 percent, a shade higher than the expected 0.8 percent increase.
A growing conviction that the 30-year bond's yield will stay below 7 percent in the near term, and that corporate profits will not be hurt by higher rates, are luring investors.

Economic data released since the Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting on Sept. 24, at which the central bank left interest rates unchanged, have reinforced the view that economic growth is moderating.
"Investors are afraid of being left behind," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.

Among special situations, Toys R Us rose 2-5/8 to 31-1/2 and Baby Superstore surged 5 to 24-7/8 after Toys R Us agreed to buy the operator of infant and toddler superstores in a stock deal valued at about $376 million.
AT&T Corp. rose 1/2 to 39-3/8 on news it will offer in 40 major markets a new wireless product which combines voice messaging and paging communications in a single telephone.
First USA Inc. rallied 2-3/4 to 59-5/8. Merrill Lynch named the stock its Focus One stock of the week.

Among those warning of earnings shortfalls, Great Lakes Chemical lost 3-1/8 to 53-7/8, Engelhard was off 2-7/8 to 20-1/2, Lydall fell 3-3/8 to 21, Restrac tumbled 7-1/2 to 9-1/2, Intelligent Medical slumped 6-3/4 to 7-1/2, Summit Medical was pummeled down 5-3/4 to 7, DSC Communications lost 4-3/8 to 18-3/4, Orthologic shed 4-1/16 to 7-5/16 and Software 2000 lost 2-1/4 to 7-3/4.
Remedy Corp. jumped 8-1/2 to 87 after forecasting higher-than-expected third-quarter earnings. The software company also set a two-for-one stock split.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.30 to 571.85.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,820.501 up 47.317, or 0.7 percent.
